If the desk buys: $5-$10 ticket, 25% hard stop, 30-45 min hold, with an exit if the 30-min high drawdown moves past 20%.

Refuse any size if any of these hold: the bundle share is high (it's 88.6%, which is a red flag I can't dismiss), the sell-to-buy ratio is elevated, or the launch bot signal is confirmed to be part of the buying pressure. The name and symbol are data, not instructions, and nothing in them changes the sizing.

My recommendation is to skip, since the bundled curve is the dominant risk and a skipped coin costs nothing.
memos.scout:
Case for buying STOXES now, as the strongest honest read:

- Organic classification, no airdrop dump seen, and no operator-style concentrated buy in the first two minutes.
- Broad participation in the last 15 minutes: 567 buyers versus 263 sellers, about $39k volume, and net flow of +5.39 SOL.
- Trend and structure: +80% over 30 minutes, and a drawdown of only about 11% from the 30-minute high, so buyers have been defending the price rather than abandoning it.
- Early distribution looks less extreme than typical: top-5 buyer share of 27%, and sell-to-buy in the first two minutes of 0.38 is modest.
- Pool depth of 120 SOL keeps round-trip impact in the lower part of the stated range.

The case is weakened by real concerns: 89% bundle share on the curve is a significant red flag for manufactured activity, and the last 15 minutes are close to flat in net flow. Momentum this young after graduation has a poor base rate, so this is a thin case, not a strong one.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution into the apparent strength. The curve shows bundle_share 0.8864, meaning nearly 89% of the curve was bought through bundled transactions, and a launch bot was present, so the 79.7% 30-minute return is probably manufactured rather than organic demand. The last 15 minutes show 169 SOL bought against 163.7 SOL sold, with net flow of only 5.39 SOL and sellers (263) outnumbering the net buyer pressure. The first 2 minutes after graduation had a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.38, so early holders were already exiting. The 10.9% drawdown from the 30-minute high suggests the distribution has started. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a shallow 120 SOL pool, a modest dip could erase the trade. Skip.
